mainTopic: Who counts as one household for עירוב and תחום: eating place vs. sleeping place, and dependents who share one table
overview: This amud asks what makes a place a person's 'home' for שבת. רב says it is where he eats (מקום פיתא), and שמואל says it is where he sleeps (מקום לינה). The גמרא defends רב against a ברייתא about field workers: they would really prefer to eat in the field, so that is their true eating place. אביי reminds his forgetful teacher רב יוסף that he himself taught רב's view, by explaining that the brothers in the משנה only receive food portions (מקבלי פרס) and eat at home. A ברייתא then argues about wives and slaves who receive portions, and the גמרא rules that a תלמיד who eats at his רבי's table needs no separate עירוב. רבה rules that a group that already joined gives one עירוב share, and he explains that the משנה's brothers need separate shares only when other residents live with them. רב ששת rules that students who sleep at their רב's house measure their תחום from there, because they would gladly eat there too (אנן סהדי). A ברייתא teaches that a father and son, or a רב and his תלמיד, living alone count as individuals. Finally, a new משנה begins: courtyards joined by an עירוב still need a שיתוף to carry in their shared מבוי.

steps.title: רב says eating place, שמואל says sleeping place
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that a person's home is where he eats. שמואל holds that it is where he sleeps.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רב said: a person's home is] the place where he eats his bread. And שמואל said: it is the place where he sleeps.
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens in the middle of a מחלוקת between רב and שמואל that began on the previous page. They disagree about which location counts as a person's 'home' for שבת rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some people eat in one place and sleep in another. רב says the eating place decides where they 'live', and שמואל says the sleeping place decides. Everything that follows next tests these two positions.

keyTerms.meaning: The place of one's bread, meaning where a person eats
The place where a person sleeps at night

phrases.english: [Rav said: it is] the place of bread (where he eats),
phrases.notes: The words 'רב אמר' appear at the end of the previous page (72b).

phrases.english: and Shmuel said: the place of sleeping.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the מחלוקת that opened on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a person's home follows where he eats. שמואל: it follows where he sleeps.
steps.whyThisMatters: This basic question shapes both עירובי חצירות (who counts as a separate household) and תחום שבת (where a person's 2,000 אמות are measured from).

steps.title: Challenge from the field workers' ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that field workers' שבת limit depends on where they usually sleep. This seems to support שמואל and contradict רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: Shepherds, fig-watchmen, guardsmen and produce-watchmen: when they usually sleep in the city, they are like the city's residents. When they usually sleep in the field, they have 2,000 אמות in every direction [from where they are].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to attack רב's view. The ברייתא seems to make the sleeping place the deciding factor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These workers eat food from the city, yet the ברייתא decides their status only by where they sleep. If eating were what counted, as רב says, they should always be treated as city residents. So the ברייתא looks like it follows שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They challenged': introduces an objection from a תנאי source
Watchmen of figs drying in the field
Guards who sit in small watch-huts
2,000 אמות in every direction (the תחום שבת)

phrases.english: They challenged: Shepherds, and fig-watchmen,
and hut-guards, and produce watchmen,
when their custom is to sleep in the city,
they are like the people of the city.
When their custom is to sleep in the field,
they have two thousand [אמות] in every direction!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's side of the מחלוקת in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a person's home is where he eats
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא assigns the workers' home by where they sleep, even though they eat city food. That points to מקום לינה, not מקום פיתא.
steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is about תחום שבת (how far one may walk), not about joining an עירוב. The same question of 'where is home' applies to both areas.

steps.title: The workers would rather eat in the field too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it is obvious these workers would prefer to have their bread brought to the field. So in truth their 'bread place' is the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, we are witnesses that if people would bring them bread over there, it would be more convenient for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by reading the ברייתא as a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These workers only eat in the city because nobody brings them food. If they could, they would eat right where they sleep and work. So their real eating place is the field, and the ברייתא fits רב after all. Sleeping is not the rule here; it just shows where they would truly want to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We are witnesses': it is obvious to everyone
Bread
It is more comfortable or preferable for them

phrases.english: There, we are witnesses
that if they would bring them bread there,
it would be more pleasing to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case: the workers' true 'eating place' is the field
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves that sleeping decides a person's home.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in the ברייתא, the deciding factor is the workers' real, preferred eating place, so רב's rule stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רב survives the challenge: 'מקום פיתא' means where a person truly wants to eat, not merely where food happens to be available.

steps.title: רב יוסף does not remember this teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says he never heard רב's ruling about the place of bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I have not heard this teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף says he does not recall ever hearing the ruling of רב. This sets up אביי's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף had forgotten much of his learning because of an illness. His statement opens a short exchange in which his student אביי shows that רב יוסף himself had taught this ruling, though in a hidden form.

keyTerms.meaning: I have not heard (it)
A teaching or halachic statement

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
I have not heard this teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending רב's ruling to asking whether that ruling was really said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף does not remember רב's teaching of מקום פיתא.

steps.title: אביי recalls the mishnah about the brothers
steps.stepSummary: אביי reminds רב יוסף that he taught this ruling in connection with the משנה about brothers who eat at their father's table but sleep in their own houses. That משנה says each brother needs his own share in the עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: You told it to us, and you told it to us on this: Brothers who were eating at their father's table and sleeping in their own houses each need [a separate share in] the עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins proving to his teacher that רב יוסף did know this teaching. He starts by quoting the משנה it was connected to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes brothers who eat at their father's table but sleep in their own homes in the same courtyard. The משנה treats each brother as his own household, so each must join the עירוב separately. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: To us
The brothers
Their father's table
The shared food that joins households so carrying is permitted on שבת

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
You yourself said it to us,
and it was on this that you said it to us:

phrases.aramaic: הָאַחִין שֶׁהָיוּ אוֹכְלִין עַל שֻׁלְחַן אֲבִיהֶן,
phrases.english: Brothers who were eating at their father's table,
and sleeping in their own houses,
need an עירוב for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְּ אֲמַרְתְּ נִיהֲלַן, וְאַהָא אֲמַרְתְּ נִיהֲלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's claim of step 4 by recalling the משנה that the teaching was tied to.
steps.raayaObject: That רב יוסף had in fact taught רב's ruling
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the brothers who eat at their father's table, as רב יוסף once explained it to his students

steps.title: The students' question: does sleeping decide?
steps.stepSummary: The students had asked רב יוסף whether the משנה proves that the sleeping place decides a person's home.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we said to you: Learn from this that the place of sleeping is what decides!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי recalls the question the students once asked about that משנה. It sounds like strong support for שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers eat with their father, yet they still count as separate households. It seems the only thing separating them is where they sleep. So the משנה appears to say that מקום לינה decides, against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Learn from it': a proposed inference
Causes or determines

phrases.english: And we said to you:
Learn from it that the place of sleeping is what determines!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's view that the eating place decides
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The brothers share their father's table but are still separate households. The only difference left is where they sleep, so sleeping must be what decides.

steps.title: The brothers only receive food portions
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף had answered, quoting רב יהודה in the name of רב, that the משנה speaks of brothers who receive food portions from their father and actually eat in their own homes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you told us about it: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: They taught this about [brothers] who receive a portion.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his reminder by quoting רב יוסף's own answer, which proves that רב יוסף knew רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers are only 'at their father's table' in the sense that he gives them food. They take that food home and eat it there. So their true eating place is their own house, which fits רב's rule. This answer only makes sense if one holds מקום פיתא, so רב יוסף must have known that teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who receive a food portion and take it to eat elsewhere
'They taught': the case the משנה is talking about
Regarding it

phrases.english: And you said to us about it,
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
They taught it about those who receive a portion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the inference of step 6 and completes אביי's proof against step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The brothers eat with their father, so sleeping must be what separates them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The brothers only receive portions and eat at home, so their eating place is their own house. This is consistent with רב.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי shows that רב יוסף himself taught רב's view (מקום פיתא) through the explanation 'מקבלי פרס'. The משנה of the brothers is no proof for שמואל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a ruling can be hidden inside an explanation of a משנה: the answer 'מקבלי פרס' is only needed if eating decides a person's home.

steps.title: A ברייתא: wives and slaves who receive food portions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings a מחלוקת about a man whose five wives and five slaves each get a food portion from him and live in their own rooms. רבי יהודה בן בתירה permits for the wives and forbids for the slaves. רבי יהודה בן בבא permits for the slaves and forbids for the wives.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A man has five wives who get food portions from their husband, and five slaves who get food portions from their master. רבי יהודה בן בתירה permits with the wives and forbids with the slaves. רבי יהודה בן בבא permits with the slaves and forbids with the wives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new case that is close to the brothers case from before. Here a whole household of wives and slaves gets food portions from one man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Permits' means these people count as part of the man's household, so they do not each need their own share in the עירוב. 'Forbids' means each one counts as living separately and must give his or her own share. רבי יהודה בן בתירה sees the wives as living with their husband, but not the slaves. רבי יהודה בן בבא sees a slave as fully tied to his master, while a wife has her own standing.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. This opens a ברייתא.
A food portion given out by the head of the house
Permits. Here it means no separate share in the עירוב is needed.
Forbids. Here it means each person must give a separate share.
Slaves

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מתיר' and 'אוסר' do not mean carrying is allowed or forbidden in general. They answer one question: does each wife or slave need his or her own share in the עירוב, or are they covered by the master of the house?
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא opens the bigger question of which kinds of dependents count as part of the main household for עירוב.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who has five wives
who receive a food portion from their husband,
phrases.notes: Each wife lives in her own room in the courtyard.

phrases.english: and five slaves
who receive a food portion from their master —

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה מַתִּיר בַּנָּשִׁים,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira permits with the wives,
phrases.notes: They count as living with their husband.

phrases.english: and forbids with the slaves.
phrases.notes: Each slave counts as living on his own.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא מַתִּיר בָּעֲבָדִים,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava permits with the slaves,
phrases.notes: A slave is fully tied to his master.

phrases.english: and forbids with the wives.
phrases.notes: Each wife has her own standing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ חָמֵשׁ נָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the brothers who get פרס from their father, the גמרא brings a parallel ברייתא about wives and slaves who get פרס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה בן בתירה: wives are covered by the husband, slaves are not. רבי יהודה בן בבא: slaves are covered by the master, wives are not.

steps.title: רב's source for רבי יהודה בן בבא: דניאל at the king's gate
steps.stepSummary: רב explains רבי יהודה בן בבא's view from the פסוק 'And Daniel was at the king's gate.' A servant of the king counts as being with the king wherever he actually is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: What is the reason of רבי יהודה בן בבא? Because it is written: 'And Daniel was at the gate of the king.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a פסוק to explain why רבי יהודה בן בבא treats slaves as part of their master's household.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes דניאל's role, not his actual place. He was the king's servant, so wherever he went he counted as being at the king's gate. The same is true of a slave. Even when he sleeps in his own room, he counts as living with his master.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
As it is written (introduces a פסוק)
At the gate of the king (Aramaic, from ספר דניאל)

phrases.english: Rav said: What is the reason
of Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava?
As it is written: "And Daniel was at the gate of the king".
phrases.notes: Daniel 2:49. Daniel counted as at the king's gate wherever he was, because he served the king.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the second opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה בן בבא's ruling that slaves are part of the master's household for עירוב
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק in דניאל: 'And Daniel was at the gate of the king'

steps.title: Summing up: son, wife, and slave
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reviews the cases so far. A son with his father is clear, as already said. A wife with her husband and a slave with his master depend on the מחלוקת in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that a son with his father follows what we already said. A wife with her husband and a slave with his master depend on the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה בן בתירה and רבי יהודה בן בבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next question. It first lists which cases are already settled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son case was settled by רב's explanation of the brothers' משנה: what counts is where they eat. The wife and slave cases are already covered by the מחלוקת in the ברייתא. Since these are known, the גמרא can now ask about a case not yet covered.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious
As we said already
A מחלוקת, a dispute

phrases.english: It is obvious: a son with his father is as we said.
phrases.notes: This refers back to the brothers' משנה and רב's explanation.

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה אֵצֶל בַּעְלָהּ וְעֶבֶד אֵצֶל רַבּוֹ,
phrases.english: A wife with her husband and a slave with his master
are the dispute of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira
and Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the son case from earlier and the wife and slave cases from the ברייתא, to prepare a new question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Son: settled by where he eats. Wife and slave: depend on the מחלוקת in the ברייתא.

steps.title: The new question: a student living with his teacher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a תלמיד who lives in his רבי's courtyard and gets food from him. Does he count as part of the רבי's household for the עירוב?
steps.simpleTranslation: A student with his teacher, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question about a case not yet covered: a תלמיד who lives with his רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תלמיד is not a son, a wife, or a slave, so none of the earlier rulings clearly covers him. He depends on his רבי for food, but he is not owned by him or married to him. The גמרא wants to know which group he belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: A student
With his teacher (or master)
What? (what is the law?)

steps.whatToRemember: Son, wife, and slave are already covered. The new question is whether a תלמיד who eats from his רבי but lives in his own room needs his own share in the עירוב. The next step answers this.

phrases.english: A student with his teacher, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He lives in the teacher's courtyard and gets food from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing the settled cases, the גמרא asks about a case still open.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a תלמיד who gets food from his רבי counts as part of the רבי's household for עירוב, or must give his own share.

steps.title: Students who eat at their teacher's table need no עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the תלמיד question from the behavior of רב and רבי חייא. Each relied on his teacher's table and made no separate עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב, when he was in רבי חייא's house, said: We do not need to make an עירוב, because we rely on רבי חייא's table. And רבי חייא, when he was in רבי's house, said: We do not need to make an עירוב, because we rely on רבי's table.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 11 by bringing a real-life example. Two great students said they needed no עירוב because they ate at their teacher's table.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 asked whether a תלמיד who lives in his רבי's courtyard and eats his food counts as part of the רבי's household. רב and רבי חייא both acted as if the answer is yes. Because they 'leaned on his table', they were treated like members of the teacher's own home, so no separate עירוב was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source to answer the question
They rely on his table, meaning they eat at his expense
To make an עירוב
In the house or school of רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that a תלמיד eating at his רבי's table is part of the רבי's household for עירוב purposes, like a son eating at his father's table.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
For Rav, in the house of Rabbi Chiyya, said:
We do not need to make an eruv,
since we rely
on the table of Rabbi Chiyya.
And Rabbi Chiyya, in the house of Rebbi, said:
We do not need to make an eruv,
since we rely
on the table of Rebbi.
phrases.notes: רבי here means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּרַב בֵּי רַבִּי חִיָּיא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 11 about a תלמיד.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A תלמיד who eats at his רבי's table counts as part of the רבי's household and needs no separate עירוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice and statements of רב at רבי חייא's house and of רבי חייא at רבי's house.

steps.title: Five residents who already joined: is one share enough for the next courtyard?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבה about five residents of one courtyard who already combined their עירוב. When they join with a different courtyard, does one share cover all five?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked רבה: Five people in one courtyard collected their עירוב together. When they bring their עירוב to another place, is one עירוב share enough for all of them, or does each one need his own share?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. אביי asks whether a group that already joined together now counts as one person when it joins with another courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five residents already made an עירוב among themselves, so inside their courtyard they act like one household. The question is whether that unity carries over when they join a second courtyard. If it does, one contribution is enough. If it does not, all five must each give a share.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him: a formal question put to a teacher
Who collected their עירוב, meaning they already joined together
Another place, here a different courtyard
For each and every one

phrases.english: Abaye asked Rabba:
Five who collected their eruv together,
when they bring their eruv to another place,
is one eruv share enough for all of them,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ צְרִיכִין עֵירוּב לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד?
phrases.english: or do they need an eruv share for each and every one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who counts as one household to a new case: a group that already joined through an עירוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a group that already combined its עירוב count as one unit when it joins another courtyard?

steps.title: רבה answers that one share covers them all
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that one עירוב share is enough for all five.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: One עירוב share is enough for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a direct answer to אביי's question. Once the five have joined, they count as one unit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה treats the joined group like a single household. So when they join a second courtyard, the group gives only one share, just as a single resident would.

keyTerms.meaning: One עירוב share for all of them

phrases.english: He said to him: One eruv share for all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One share covers the whole group that already joined.

steps.title: Challenge from the brothers in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה from the brothers in the משנה. They are like a group that collected together, yet the משנה says each one needs his own share.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about brothers, who are like people who collected their עירוב together? And yet the משנה teaches: they need an עירוב share for each and every one!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's answer using our own משנה. The brothers seem to be one group, yet the משנה demands a share from each brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers all eat from their father's food, so they look like a joined group, just like the five residents. If a joined group needs only one share, the brothers should need only one share too. But the משנה says each brother must give his own, which seems to contradict רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: But look: opens a challenge
Brothers
They are similar
And yet it teaches, pointing to the source's wording

phrases.english: But look at the brothers,
who are like those who collected together,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָתָנֵי: צְרִיכִין עֵירוּב לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד!
phrases.english: and yet it teaches: they need an eruv share for each and every one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that one share covers a joined group.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The brothers in the משנה are like a joined group, yet the משנה requires a share from each of them.

steps.title: The משנה speaks of a courtyard with other residents
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the משנה speaks of a case where other residents live with the brothers. Because those residents forbid carrying, the brothers forbid it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A case where other residents live with them. Since these residents forbid carrying, those brothers also forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends his ruling by limiting the משנה to a special case. In the משנה, the brothers share the courtyard with other residents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When other residents live in the same courtyard, they cause a prohibition on carrying until everyone joins. Since those residents forbid, the brothers are also counted as separate people who forbid. So each brother needs his own share, but a group living alone would need only one share, as רבה said.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Limits a source to a specific case
Residents, here other people living in the courtyard
Since: because of one fact, another follows
They forbid carrying

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying the brothers stop being one family. He is saying that when outsiders live in the courtyard, the brothers are also treated as separate people for this עירוב.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
For example, where there are other residents with them.
Since these residents forbid,
those brothers also forbid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה requires a share from each brother in every situation, which would contradict רבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks only of a courtyard with other residents. Because they forbid, the brothers forbid too. Without outside residents, one share is enough.

steps.title: The משנה's own wording supports רבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves רבה's reading from the end of the משנה. It says that if there are no other residents in the courtyard, the brothers do not need an עירוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it is reasonable, because the משנה teaches: When is this so? When they bring their עירוב to another place. But if their עירוב comes to them, or if there are no other residents with them in the courtyard, they do not need to make an עירוב. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבה's answer from the words of the משנה. It then closes with שמע מינה, meaning the point is proven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the משנה says that if no other residents live with the brothers, no עירוב is needed at all. This shows that the earlier rule, a share from each brother, was only for a courtyard with other residents. That is exactly what רבה said.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is reasonable: introduces support for the last answer
When? The source limits when its rule applies
In the courtyard
Learn from this: the point is proven

steps.whatToRemember: A group that lives together as one unit gives one עירוב share. The משנה's demand for a share from each brother applies only when other residents also live in the courtyard.
steps.whyThisMatters: This confirms רבה's rule and makes clear exactly when the brothers in the משנה need separate shares.

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
as it teaches: When is this so?

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁמּוֹלִיכִין אֶת עֵירוּבָן בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר,
phrases.english: When they bring their eruv to another place,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִם הָיָה עֵירוּבָן בָּא אֶצְלָם,
phrases.english: but if their eruv was coming to them,
or if there are no other residents with them in the courtyard,
they do not need to make an eruv.
Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 16 from the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's answer that the משנה speaks of a courtyard with other residents.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the משנה: if no other residents live with them, they need no עירוב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The requirement for each brother to give a share applies only when other residents share the courtyard. Otherwise the group counts as one.

steps.title: Students who eat in one place and sleep in another
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין asks רב ששת: students eat bread in their own houses in the field and sleep in the house of their רב. Do we measure their תחום from the רב's house or from the field?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בר אבין asked רב ששת: The students of the בית המדרש eat their bread in the field, and then come and sleep in the רב's house. When we measure their שבת limit, do we measure it from the רב's house or from the field?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question about the שבת limit (תחום). It wants to know which place counts as a person's home: where he eats or where he sleeps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's תחום of 2000 אמה is measured from his home. These students have two 'homes': they eat in one place and sleep in another. The question is which of the two activities sets the person's location.

keyTerms.meaning: Students of the study hall, who stay in the house of their רב
A field or open area; here, where the students' own houses are
The שבת limit, 2000 אמה from one's place
We measure

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Avin asked of Rav Sheshet:

phrases.aramaic: בְּנֵי בֵי רַב, דְּאָכְלִי נַהֲמָא בְּבָאגָא,
phrases.english: Students of the master's house, who eat bread in the field,
and come and sleep in the master's house,
when we measure the Shabbos limit for them,
do we measure it for them from the master's house
or do we measure it for them from the field?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a related but new question. After the earlier steps about who counts as one household for עירוב, the גמרא now asks what counts as a person's place of residence for the תחום.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a person's place for the תחום set by where he sleeps or by where he eats?

steps.title: We measure from where they sleep
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the תחום is measured from the רב's house, where the students sleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We measure from the רב's house.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question. The students' שבת limit is measured from the place where they sleep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this answer, the sleeping place sets a person's home for the תחום, not the eating place. This sets up the next challenge, because in another case the eating place seems to decide.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him (introduces the answer)

phrases.english: He said to him: We measure from the master's house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תחום is measured from the רב's house, where the students sleep.

steps.title: Challenge from an עירוב placed away from home
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אבין challenges the answer. With עירוב תחומין, a person puts his food within 2000 אמה and goes home to sleep, yet his תחום is measured from the עירוב. That shows the eating place decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at a person who places his עירוב within 2000 אמה and then comes home and sleeps in his house. We measure his שבת limit from his עירוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is challenged from the case of עירוב תחומין. There, the place of the food (the meal) decides a person's location, not the place where he sleeps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב תחומין is food set down as a 'meal' to make that spot a person's Shabbos home. Even though he sleeps at home, his תחום is measured from the food. So it seems the eating place matters, which goes against רב ששת's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: But look! (opens a challenge from a known case)
Food placed to set a new שבת home for measuring the תחום
2000 אמה, the size of the שבת limit
He sleeps / spends the night

steps.confusionAlert: The person in this case actually sleeps at home, yet his תחום still starts from the עירוב. That is exactly why it seems to contradict רב ששת.

phrases.english: But behold, one who places his eiruv
within two thousand cubits,
and comes and sleeps in his house,
that we measure his Shabbos limit from his eiruv!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲרֵי נוֹתֵן אֶת עֵירוּבוֹ בְּתוֹךְ אַלְפַּיִם אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 19 using the accepted law of עירוב תחומין.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling that the sleeping place decides the תחום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With עירוב תחומין the meal place sets the תחום even though the person sleeps at home. So the eating place should decide for the students too.

steps.title: In each case we go by what the person really wants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in both cases 'we are witnesses' to the person's true wishes. The one who placed an עירוב would rather stay by his עירוב. The students would rather eat in the רב's house if bread were brought there.
steps.simpleTranslation: In that case we are witnesses, and in this case we are witnesses. In that case we are witnesses that if he could stay there by his עירוב, he would like it. In this case we are witnesses that if they brought the students bread in the רב's house, they would like it even more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Both cases follow one rule: a person's home is the place where he truly wants to be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same אנן סהדי reasoning the גמרא used for the field workers in step 3. The man with the עירוב wants to be near his עירוב, since he plans to walk on from there, so it counts as his home. The students would gladly eat in the רב's house if bread were brought there, so their true eating place, and their home, is the רב's house. This fits רב's rule of מקום פיתא, understood as where a person truly wants to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: We are witnesses: it is obvious to everyone what the person wants
To stay / reside
It is pleasing to him; he would prefer it
Bread
More

steps.whatToRemember: For the תחום, a person's 'home' is where he truly wants to be (אנן סהדי). It is not set by eating alone or by sleeping alone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that residence in הלכות שבת can depend on a person's clear true wishes, not only on his physical actions.

phrases.english: In that case, we are witnesses,
and in this case, we are witnesses.
In that case we are witnesses

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי מִיתְּדַר לֵיהּ הָתָם נִיחָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: that if he could reside there, it would please him,
and in this case we are witnesses

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי מַיְיתוּ לְהוּ רִיפְתָּא לְבֵי רַב,
phrases.english: that if they would bring them bread to the master's house,
it would please them more.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהָהוּא אֲנַן סָהֲדִי וּבְהָדָא אֲנַן סָהֲדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 20 by showing both cases follow one principle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Unifying principle: both cases follow the person's evident true wishes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the עירוב case proves that the eating place always decides residence.
steps.terutzMaskana: Residence follows where the person clearly wants to be. For the students, that is the רב's house, where they sleep.

steps.title: Do a father and son count as many people or as one?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks רב חסדא whether a father and son, or a רב and his תלמיד, count as many people or as individuals. Do they need an עירוב? Can their מבוי be permitted with a לחי and קורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked רב חסדא: A father and his son, or a רב and his תלמיד: are they like many people or like individuals? Do they need an עירוב or not? Is their alleyway permitted with a side post and cross beam, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about whether certain close pairs count as one unit or as separate people. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many people sharing a space need an עירוב, and a lone individual does not. A father and son, or a רב and his תלמיד, are two people, but one leans on the other. The question has two practical effects: whether they need an עירוב, and whether a לחי or קורה alone permits their מבוי, or whether it also needs a שיתוף as separate households would.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked (raised a question)
Are they like many people?
Are they like individuals?
An alleyway shared by courtyards
A side post and a cross beam that permit carrying in a מבוי

steps.confusionAlert: Being treated 'as individuals' is the lenient outcome for both questions. They would need no עירוב, and a לחי or קורה alone would permit their מבוי without a שיתוף. Being treated as 'many' would mean they need an עירוב, and their מבוי would need a שיתוף in addition to the לחי or קורה. The next step's ברייתא rules that they count as individuals.

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked of Rav Chisda:
A father and his son, a master and his student,
are they like many people or like individuals?

phrases.aramaic: צְרִיכִין עֵירוּב, אוֹ אֵין צְרִיכִין עֵירוּב?
phrases.english: Do they need an eiruv, or do they not need an eiruv?
Is their alleyway permitted by a side post and cross beam,
or is it not permitted by a side post and cross beam?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא מֵרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תחום discussion and returns to the earlier theme from steps 13 to 17: when several people count as one unit for עירוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do a father and son, or a רב and his תלמיד, count as many people or as individuals? This decides whether they need an עירוב and whether a לחי or קורה permits their מבוי.

steps.title: רב חסדא answers from a ברייתא: they count as individuals
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא tells רמי בר חמא that the answer is already taught in a ברייתא. A father and son, or a רב and his תלמיד, with no other residents, count as individuals. They need no עירוב, and their מבוי is permitted with a לחי or קורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: You already learned this. A father and his son, or a teacher and his student, when no other residents live with them, are treated like individuals. They do not need to make an עירוב, and their alleyway becomes permitted with a side post or a cross beam.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question from Step 22 by quoting a ברייתא that already settles it. A father and son, or a רב and his תלמיד, count as one unit, not as many people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These pairs are so closely tied that the הלכה treats them like one household. So there is no group of separate households that would need an עירוב to join together. Their מבוי is treated like one person's alley, so a לחי or קורה is enough and no שיתוף is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: You have already learned it (in a ברייתא)
Residents; other people living with them
Individuals; treated as a single unit
To make an עירוב

steps.whatToRemember: A father and son, or a רב and his תלמיד, living alone together, count as one unit. They need no עירוב, and a לחי or קורה permits their מבוי.
steps.confusionAlert: The rule holds only when no other residents live with them. If other residents are there, they no longer count as a single unit, and the usual rules apply.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the הלכה looks at how closely people's lives are tied together, not just at how many people there are.

phrases.english: He (Rav Chisda) said to him: You have learned it:
phrases.notes: The answer is already in a ברייתא you've learned.

phrases.english: A father and his son, a teacher and his student,
when there are no other residents with them,
they are considered like individuals,
and they do not need to make an eiruv,
and their alleyway becomes permitted with a side post or cross beam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רמי בר חמא's question in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a father and son, or a רב and his תלמיד, count as many people or as individuals for עירוב and for the מבוי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They count as individuals when no other residents live with them. They need no עירוב, and their מבוי is permitted with a לחי or קורה.

steps.title: New משנה: five connected courtyards that also open to an alley
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes five courtyards that open into each other and into a מבוי. If they made an עירוב חצירות but no שיתוף in the מבוי, they may carry in the courtyards but not in the מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Five courtyards open into one another and also open into an alleyway. If they made an עירוב for the courtyards but did not make a שיתוף for the alleyway, they may carry in the courtyards and may not carry in the alleyway.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new case. Five courtyards are joined to each other and also open onto a shared alley.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עירוב חצירות joins the courtyards, so carrying among them is permitted. The alley is a separate area that needs its own joining, called a שיתוף מבואות. Since none was made, carrying in the מבוי stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
Courtyards
The joining that permits carrying between houses and courtyards
They joined in a שיתוף, the merging that permits carrying in the מבוי
An alleyway shared by several courtyards

steps.confusionAlert: An עירוב חצירות and a שיתוף מבואות are two separate things. Making one does not cover the other. That is exactly why the courtyards are permitted here while the מבוי is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the משנה and the גמרא's discussion of when one type of joining can or cannot do the job of the other.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Five courtyards that open into one another
and also open into an alleyway,
if they made an eiruv in the courtyards
but did not merge (make a shituf) in the alleyway,
they are permitted to carry in the courtyards
and forbidden to carry in the alleyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ חָמֵשׁ חֲצֵירוֹת פְּתוּחוֹת זוֹ לָזוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It does not depend on the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עירוב חצירות without a שיתוף מבואות permits carrying in the courtyards but not in the מבוי.
